summary: Degrade and priority inheritance are unreconciled; PriorityInheritingLock restores a pre-boost priority on unlock so a degrade applied to a boosted holder is silently undone, and degrading a boosted task discards a boost a waiter depends on. summary: GICC_PMR's implemented priority width was compiled in, not discovered, and the first silicon disproved it: gic.rs declares PRIORITY_MASK_ALL = 0xF8 with the comment "GIC-400 implements 32 priority levels, so the low three bits read as zero", writes it, and refuses routing unless readback & 0xF8 == 0xF8. BOARD VERDICT 5 read back 0xF0, so the virtual-timer PPI was refused as MaskNotHeld(0xF0) and STORY-P1-07-04 criterion 1 (tick count, rmin/rmax) has no evidence. 0xF0 is conformant: GICv2 leaves unimplemented low-order priority bits RAZ/WI with the implemented bits contiguous from bit 7 down, so 0xF0 means BCM2712 implements four priority bits (16 levels), the architectural minimum, not five. The code refused a conforming device. Same class as the three ethernet cures (outbound window, endpoint BARs, inbound windows): device state that must be read, not assumed. Fixing it as 0xF8 -> 0xF0 is barred - that substitutes one board's measured value for another guess and violates the no-bench-tuned-constants rule
origin: BOARD VERDICT 5 (TinyOS measure boot 2026-08-04), TOS64-TICK/1 REFUSED=GICC-PMR READBACK=000000F0
owner_path: Discover the width instead of asserting it: write all ones to GICC_PMR and take the readback as the widest legal open mask for that implementation; gate on conformance of shape (implemented bits a contiguous run ending at bit 7, at least four of them per GICv2) rather than equality against a constant; carry the discovered mask into the tick evidence line so the width is recorded per board rather than assumed per family; re-run the measure boot and read a live TOS64-TICK/1 with its ratio bounds

summary: The boot epoch STORY-P1-10-04 puts in every spoor frame is a distinguisher, not an identifier. It is derived from CNTVCT_EL0 at kernel entry, so it differs between boots only because firmware timing differs between boots -- there is no persistent store and no RTC on the Pi 5 path to derive anything stronger from. Two boots whose firmware happened to take the same number of counter ticks to reach the kernel produce the same epoch and a host reads them as one boot. A host can therefore conclude "this is a different boot" with high probability and can never conclude "this is boot number N" or "I missed exactly two boots", and the field must never be documented as though it could MEASURED 2026-08-05 and it is thinner than this row assumed: three consecutive boots of fd966f7514e4 produced epochs 0x049F8B28, 0x04B328BC and 0x04B32825. The last two differ by 0x97 = 151 counter ticks, which at 54 MHz is 2.8 MICROSECONDS - two power cycles put the kernel entry point within three microseconds of the same counter reading, so only the low byte of the epoch moved. The first pair differ by ~1.28M ticks (~23 ms), so the variation is not uniform, but a pair landing 151 ticks apart makes collision a plausible event rather than a theoretical one and a collision reads as 'same boot' to every host. BOARD VERDICTS 11-13 still stand - those epochs did differ and were read as different - so this bounds the field's future use rather than retracting any result: sound as a bench-session change detector, never an identifier, and any host or document treating it as one is wrong by measurement now and not merely by caution THIRD MEASUREMENT 2026-08-05/06, and it removes the last intuition that made this row survivable: epoch 0x04B1CA6E (BOARD VERDICT 14) to 0x04B1DF41 on the SAME board is 0x14D3 = 5331 counter ticks = about 99 MICROSECONDS at 54 MHz - and those two boots were separated by HOURS, not by a back-to-back power cycle. The two earlier pairs were 151 ticks (2.8 us) and about 1.28M ticks (23 ms), both from rapid cycles, which left open the reading that a long gap makes a collision unlikely. It does not. The entropy is NOT a function of how long the board was off, because the counter this epoch is derived from is reset by the firmware on every boot rather than free-running across power - so the value is a measure of firmware-handoff-to-kernel-entry latency, which is precisely the quantity this system is engineered to make repeatable. The better the boot path gets, the WORSE the epoch gets as an identifier
owner_path: BCM2712 has a hardware RNG (rng200) that would make the epoch a genuine nonce, and firmware-persisted state would make it a genuine counter; both are their own device bring-up and neither is in FEAT-P1-10. Until one exists, every document and every host tool states the epoch as a change detector rather than as a boot number

summary: TinyOS drives the Pi 5 with no thermal awareness of any kind: it never reads the SoC temperature sensor, has no throttle path, and does not program RP1 PWM, so the fan connector is dead on every TinyOS boot. Observed by the owner during the STORY-P1-10-04 board session on 2026-08-05 - the fan spins immediately under Pi OS (Linux binds pwm-fan to a thermal zone and sets the duty cycle from the measured temperature) and never spins under TinyOS. This is not a defect in any Story; it is an absence nothing has ever owned. It touches rule 1 of agent.md - safety before security before correctness before performance - and the honest statement of the current position is that thermal management on this board is entirely the firmware's, TinyOS neither cooperates with it nor knows whether it is happening. Board sessions to date are 30-90 second captures and nothing about them is evidence for sustained operation; hand-2026-08-04/05A recorded the board left "powered, beaconing" between sessions, which is the shape of unattended continuous running that this row argues against until the gap is closed CALIBRATION ROUTE CLOSED 2026-08-05: the raw AVS datum cannot be read under Pi OS at all. /dev/mem mmap at 0x107d542000 returns EINVAL under STRICT_DEVMEM, and the only other route - the syscon debugfs regmap at /sys/kernel/debug/regmap/dummy-avs-monitor@0x000000107d542000/registers - RESET THE BOARD when read, because the region is 0xf0000 bytes and the kernel materialises ~983000 register reads before any truncation applies (SSH dropped mid-read; /proc/uptime read 110 s afterwards). Do not repeat it. So the two-point fit this row asked for is not obtainable from Linux on this card, and the honest position is PUBLISHED CONSTANTS CORROBORATED ON THIS BOARD rather than independently derived: BOARD VERDICT 14 shows the raw datum falling monotonically 758->746 as the die warms with validity bit 16 set throughout, deriving 40.9->46.7 C from cold against 38.05 C measured under Pi OS at idle. That is corroboration and is not a calibration; Ti64Dink keeps the unverified marker until a route to the raw value exists - a kernel module, a different kernel config, or reading it from TinyOS at a temperature Linux independently reports
origin: Owner observation during the BOARD VERDICT 11-13 session, 2026-08-05
owner_path: Two separable pieces, sensing before actuation. First, read the temperature: transcribe the BCM2712 thermal sensor from the Pi OS ground truth already captured in this file and put the reading on the spoor stream as its own rung, so the board can say how hot it is before anything tries to act on it. Second, drive the fan from that reading through RP1 PWM - derived from the measured temperature and never a hardcoded duty cycle, the discipline LE-69 was closed under. Until the first piece exists, the operational rule is that the board is powered for a run and powered down after it, and no document claims anything about sustained thermal behaviour

summary: The TOS64-MEAS/2 measurement envelope rides the wire as a CYCLING TEXT TRANSCRIPT with none of the guarantees the spoor channel next to it has, and the gap is structural rather than cosmetic. A spoor frame carries a 64-bit sequence, a boot epoch, a record count and a flags word, so loss is an exact count, boots are distinguishable, order is guaranteed and the boot prologue is retained for a late listener. A transcript line carries NOTHING - no sequence, no epoch, no framing - because it predates the spoor substrate and was built as FEAT-P1-09/STORY-P1-07-06 bring-up evidence. Three consequences, all observed on 2026-08-05: a capture starting mid-cycle sees a ROTATION of the envelope rather than the envelope, and xtask parse-meas rightly refuses it (no BEGIN before the first record); a lost line is INVISIBLE because there is no gap accounting on this channel; and a capture spanning a reboot would interleave two boots envelopes with nothing to tell them apart. Ti64Dink recovers order today by filtering to TOS64-MEAS/2 lines and rotating so BEGIN is first, which is exact - but it rests on an ASSUMPTION ABOUT THE EMITTER (that BEGIN is line 0 of the cycle) rather than on a property of the wire, which is precisely the class of assumption LE-69, LE-71 and LE-74 were each raised over SHARPENED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-05: the retention gap is not only about a mid-cycle start, it silently costs the ONLY verdict the channel carries. A wire harvest of this envelope now parses completely -- 11 metrics, BEGIN through END, every field, parser unchanged, STORY-P1-07-06 criterion 1 met -- and xtask parse-meas STILL exits 1, because the fixture emits its TOS64-RESULT/1 verdict ONCE at completion and a late listener attaching thousands of beats later can never see it. So the channel delivers every measurement and loses the pass/fail statement about them, and the exit code that reports this is indistinguishable from a failed parse. Two independent captures minutes apart rotated to BYTE-IDENTICAL envelopes, which is the good half: the rotation is exact. But exactness of the rotation is not retention, and the retained boot certificate STORY-P1-10-04 built for the spoor channel is precisely the mechanism this channel lacks

owner_path: Carry the envelope as SPOORS rather than as text: one record per metric with the value in the cost field, at which point it inherits sequence, epoch, exact loss accounting and retention for free, and the boot certificate mechanism STORY-P1-10-04 already built could retain the envelope so a late listener receives it whole - the same problem, already solved once on the other channel. summary: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` reports success-or-failure for the workspace but does NOT lint the whole workspace when any crate fails to compile: cargo stops at the first failure and every package after it goes unlinted, silently. On this Windows bench `kernel`s [[bin]] names `hal_x86_64` items gated cfg(not(windows)) so it cannot compile at all, which means the workspace run has been dying at `kernel` and never reaching the crates after it -- for the entire life of the bench. Proved by an `unused import: crate::board` in hal-arm64/src/thermal.rs that passed every local gate and was caught only by CI on Linux (run 31012173030, the first red push since LE-72 closed). This is LE-64s Windows-host-blindness class in a new form: LE-64 and LE-72 are both about code the host cannot COMPILE, and this is about code the host silently never LINTS because something earlier failed. The lesson generalises past clippy -- any batch command that stops on first failure reports on a prefix of its subject while appearing to report on all of it

summary: Every board image this project cites by hash is an identifier for an artifact NOBODY RETAINED and that CANNOT BE REBUILT. Seventeen documents across goals/ and session/ name images by hash (0c709197ed26, fd966f7514e4, 92fa283a6d20, f8133b0958d3) as though the hash resolved to something, and none of them does: os/target/pi5/kernel8.img is a SINGLE PATH that every variant build overwrites, so at most one image exists at a time and building any fixture destroys the last one. The only other copy has been the TFTP root, which hand-2026-08-05/05A itself calls transient. And the images are not byte-reproducible across tree states: rebuilding the measure fixture on 2026-08-05 after the thermal and board_dispatch work produced f370cbf6bc05, not the 92fa283a6d20 the same subcommand produced earlier the same day, because the tree moved. So an image hash in a Report is not a reference, it is a number, and a third party asked to reproduce a run cannot obtain the binary that produced it. This is the LE-74 defect one layer out: LE-74 bounds the boot EPOCH as a change detector rather than an identifier, and this row says the same of the IMAGE HASH, which every Report has been treating as the stronger of the two
origin: FOUND BY DESTROYING ONE, 2026-08-05, and recorded that way deliberately. An agent session read two differing kernel8.img in C:/tmp/tftproot, judged the root-level one stale leftover, and overwrote it to remove an unverifiable variable from the mandate one-shot power cycle. It was not stale: hand-2026-08-05/04A section 6 records 92fa283a6d20 as the measure fixture image and the last image, and it is the image the board is currently executing. The overwrite was reasoned but rested on an assumption about a file rather than a check of the record, and the file it destroyed was the only copy. Impact is bounded and stated rather than minimised: the directory is documented transient, the root path is not the boot path (the firmware requests the 7bf18f79/ prefix), that image results are already recorded in BOARD VERDICT 14 and REPORT-2026-08-04-01, and the mandate own image f8133b0958d3 was intact throughout and now sits on all three paths. What was lost is a binary, not evidence. What it exposed is that losing it was always possible and nothing anywhere would have noticed
owner_path: An image store keyed by content hash that a build writes to and never overwrites, so os/target/pi5/kernel8.img becomes the LATEST rather than the ONLY, and a hash cited in a Report resolves to a file. Cheap: images are ~290 KB and a bench session produces a handful. Until it exists, every document citing an image hash states that the binary is not retained, exactly as LE-74 forced every document citing the epoch to state what it is not. Second and separable: whether a variant build should be byte-reproducible from a recorded tree state at all, which is a real question about the toolchain and not merely about storage, and which SEC-01 already bounds since an image that cannot be reproduced cannot be independently integrity-checked either

summary: A rung the kernel stamps can be invisible to the host decoder, and the failure presents as THE BOARD NOT DOING THE THING. kernel::spoor_stream::Rung is mirrored in TWO places in work/tools/ti64dink/Program.cs, and on 2026-08-05 both were stale in the same way. (1) The rung name table stopped at ThermalSample=8 while the kernel had added DispatchRound=9, under a doc comment asserting it is 'one table for both directions ... so the two cannot drift apart' -- an assertion with no test behind it, which had drifted. (2) A SECOND, separate hand-kept list guarded which categories carry a rung (cat is 6 or 7 or 10 -- Boot, Fault, Thermal), written before DispatchRound existed and never updated; Dispatch was absent from it. summary: tos64-netboot CRASHED ON THE FIRST PACKET IT EVER ANSWERED, and the mechanism is a fail-safe violation rather than a configuration mistake. It resolves its own server address at STARTUP via GuessLinkLocalAddress(), but the bench link comes up when the BOARD does -- so on a run started before power-on, no interface is Up with a 169.254/16 address, the guess returns IPAddress.Any, the tool prints 'server address : 0.0.0.0', offers siaddr 0.0.0.0, and then throws SocketException 10065 (no route to host) sending the broadcast reply from a socket bound to 0.0.0.0 across a host holding five IPv4 addresses. The throw was UNHANDLED inside DhcpLoop, so the entire server died on the first DISCOVER it received -- from the one MAC it exists to answer. agent.md rule 6 is fail-safe over keep-trying; a bench tool that exits on one failed send, when the client will retry DISCOVER anyway, is neither. The general shape: a program that samples an environment fact once, at the moment that fact is least likely to be true, and treats a recoverable I/O failure as fatal

summary: tos64-netboot REFUSED A LEGITIMATE TFTP REQUEST AS A PATH TRAVERSAL, and the failure presented as a kernel fault on the board. The Pi 5 firmware fetches config.txt bare at one boot stage and /config.txt -- with a leading slash -- at a later one. TFTP has no concept of an absolute path, so a leading slash is a client spelling the root, not escaping it; but Path.Combine(root, "/config.txt") DISCARDS the root and yields C:\config.txt, which the traversal guard then correctly refused. The later stage therefore never received its settings, pciex4_reset=0 among them, so the firmware reset the RP1 PCIe link. TinyOS then reported the honest consequence and reported it well: confession code 2 (LinkAbsent::PhyDown) with detail 0xE080 -- PORT_IS_RC set, PHY_LINK_UP clear -- which decodes to the PCIe link between BCM2712 and RP1 never training, and since RP1 carries the Ethernet the board went silent. The kernel was blameless and said so precisely; the log line that mattered read REFUSED: outside the tftp root and was six lines above the boot that failed. GENERAL SHAPE: a tool that refuses valid work and logs the refusal as a SECURITY event sends the operator to look at the wrong subsystem, because a security refusal reads as deliberate

summary: THE BOARD MEASURED PERF-D07-G23 CORRECTLY AND THE TRANSPORT DROPPED THE ANSWER. hal_arm64::transcript's TRANSCRIPT_CAPACITY was a hand-picked 2048 bytes under a doc comment reading 'the envelope is ~11 lines of <= 140 bytes'. Adding a twelfth metric -- the G23 spoor-enabled arm, whose name pool_u64x64_alloc_free_round_trip_per_op_of_8_spoored is the longest in the set and whose line is 169 bytes on the wire -- pushed the envelope past 2048. The buffer dropped the overflow exactly as designed, so the arm's line reached the host carrying its NAME AND NONE OF ITS NUMBERS and the END metrics=12 line never arrived at all. The fixture had run correctly on silicon; a reader comparing the two arms would have found one of them absent. THE DESIGN IS WHY THIS WAS DIAGNOSABLE IN ONE CAPTURE: the buffer's own doc promises 'overflow is dropped, never wrapped -- a truncated transcript reads as truncated, a wrapped one lies', and a wrapped buffer would have produced a plausible envelope with a wrong tail instead. GENERAL SHAPE: a capacity that is a constant BESIDE its consumers rather than a function OF them goes stale the moment anyone adds a line, and nothing fails until a board run does

Two tests guard it and BOTH WERE SEEN TO FAIL against the old 2048 before being trusted: one records MAX_LINES lines of MAX_LINE_BYTES and asserts the LAST line survives whole, because truncation eats the tail first; one replays the exact twelve-metric envelope that broke it. summary: NOTHING MACHINE-CHECKS WHICH PERFORMANCE DOMAIN A FIXTURE METRIC IS LABELLED WITH, so a metric can be labelled to fit the contract its Story happens to select rather than to name its own subject -- and when that happens the number is never read against the gate whose subject it is. D07 is fixed-capacity pool allocation; D11 is spoor stamp and journal, which is exactly and only what those three measure. The numbers were on the wire, quoted in a Report, a handover and the Story's own status header, and NOT ONCE COMPARED TO D11'S TARGETS -- which the stamp misses by 1.90x at the median (PERF-D11-G01, filed 2026-08-06). The label is what decides which target column a measurement is read against, so a wrong label is not a naming defect, it is an unread gate. summary: THE 0 OF 99 ASSURANCE-VERIFIED FIGURE IS ARITHMETICALLY LOCKED AND NOTHING RECORDS THAT IT IS. The register presents it as a progress metric beside genuine progress metrics, and every Report in the tree attributes it to LE-09 hardware debt, which is a different and less blocking thing. Related: the evidence vocabulary is measured/refused/structural with open-debt beside it and there is NO WAY TO RECORD THAT A GUARDRAIL DOES NOT APPLY TO A STORY, so even a Story with no bound to state owes a G04 it can never close. Whether that absence is a defect or a deliberate anti-waiver property is a design question this row does not presume to answer

summary: A MANUAL POWER CYCLE IS THE ONLY UNBUILT STAGE OF THE BOARD EVIDENCE LOOP, AND IT IS WHAT STALLS THE PROJECT. As of 2026-08-06 nine of the ten stages are built and proven -- image build, staged digest verification, netboot service, a log readable live, waiting for a board event via ti64dink --until, envelope capture, TRANSMITTING to the board via ti64dink --send, parse-meas, and the timing gate. The tenth is a human hand on a mains plug. The consequence is measurable rather than theoretical: release-gate evidence has not moved from 23 since 02A, two consecutive sessions ended built-gated-and-unmeasured, and 03B section 6 item 1 -- costed at twenty minutes with the image already staged -- has now survived two sessions with the digest byte-identical throughout. An agent session optimises for what it can finish, so it builds the thing whose last step is a laptop command and writes a handover whose item 1 nobody can take. This also gates ADR 0005 Q3, which is a RESIDENCY CAMPAIGN WITH A STATED DURATION: a campaign is exactly what a manual bench cannot run, so the single locked gate behind 0/99 (LE-94) is downstream of a power switch
owner_path: TOOL BUILT 2026-08-06 IN THE SAME SESSION THIS WAS RAISED; THE PURCHASE IS THE REMAINING HALF AND IT IS THE OWNERS. tos64-power (work/tools/power/, the sdprep pattern) drives four LAN dialects with no vendor cloud account -- Tasmota, Shelly gen1, Shelly gen2 and ESPHome -- chosen so the bench buys whichever is in stock rather than one named product. All four clauses of the fail-safe contract are pure functions with tests rather than careful code, because a fail-safe whose only test is a real board on a real relay is a fail-safe this project cannot afford to test: it owns one Pi 5. (1) never leave the board off -- PowerPolicy.OwesRestore over every cycle phase, with an UNCONFIRMED off treated as off, three bounded restore attempts and then exit 4, a code no other outcome shares; (2) refuse mid-transfer -- TransferGuard against a marker tos64-netboot now writes per acknowledged block, where an unreadable marker is Unknown and Unknown refuses; (3) bounds refused rather than clamped, off-interval [1000, 60000] ms and on-wait [1, 600] s; (4) a readback decides and nothing else does -- Shelly gen2s Switch.Set answers was_on, the PREVIOUS state, and there is no was_on key in the reader on purpose. xtask board-run composes all ten stages, with the ordering as a VALUE (board_run::plan) rather than as control flow, because these orderings are safety properties on a mains path and a safety property expressed as the shape of a function is one nobody can test: every plan ends with the board ON, the digest is checked before anything is served, the server is up before power moves. 99 C# tests, 9 Rust tests, ELEVEN mutations applied and each seen to fail on its named test. WHAT REMAINS IS ONE PURCHASE, about 15 pounds, and it is 05C section 5 decision 3

summary: THE BOARD-RUN EXECUTOR HAS NEVER RUN AGAINST A PLUG, AND IT IS THE ONLY PART OF THE POWER PATH THAT IS NOT TESTED. board_run::plan is a pure function with nine host tests carrying every ordering invariant, and tos64-powers four fail-safe clauses are pure functions with 99 tests and an eleven-mutation falsification sweep -- but board_run::execute spawns dotnet run for tos64-netboot, tos64-power and ti64dink and nothing has ever observed it do so. The untested surface was deliberately made as small as it could be rather than eliminated, because eliminating it needs the relay LE-95 is waiting on. THE SPECIFIC UNPROVEN CLAIMS, listed so the first real run is a checklist rather than a discovery: that dotnet run --project passes the child exit code through unchanged, which is what distinguishes exit 4 (the board may be dark) from any other failure; that killing the netboot child leaves UDP 67/69 clear for the next run, which LE-87 says is the difference between a fresh image and a stale one; that ti64dink --until returns while the board is still beaconing rather than after the window; and that the transfer marker written per acknowledged block is visible to a SEPARATE PROCESS in time to refuse a cycle -- the guard is tested against strings, not against a live server. ALSO UNPROVEN BY CONSTRUCTION: the four plug dialects are asserted against their published HTTP shapes and against a loopback fake, never against firmware. A dialect that is wrong about a real device fails at the readback, which is the safe direction, but it fails as UNKNOWN rather than as a wrong dialect
owner_path: The first powered run discharges most of it and costs nothing extra: board-run --dry-run already prints the plan, so the first real invocation should be a cycle with no image staged and no watch, which exercises the power legs and the exit-code path with nothing to lose if the board does not come up. Then a full run. The marker-visibility claim wants its own check -- start tos64-netboot, request the image, and run tos64-power off against the live root, expecting exit 1

summary: tos64-netboot FELL BACK TO 0.0.0.0 AS ITS SERVER ADDRESS AND WOULD HAVE POISONED THE BOOT, CAUGHT THIRTY SECONDS BEFORE POWER-ON. GuessLinkLocalAddress takes the first 169.254.x.x on an interface that is UP, and the bench Ethernet is DISCONNECTED until the board powers -- link needs a powered far end -- so on 2026-08-06 the guess found nothing and IPAddress.Any went into the DHCP OFFER. The board would have been told siaddr=0.0.0.0 and option 66 = 0.0.0.0, would have failed to fetch, and WOULD HAVE LOOKED LIKE A BOARD FAULT. That is the seventh instrument failure wearing a device failure's costume. The failure is silent by construction: the tool PRINTS the address it chose and prints it as confidently for 0.0.0.0 as for a real one. WORSE ONCE THE LINK IS UP: this laptop carries FOUR link-local addresses -- Ethernet, Bluetooth PAN and two virtual adapters -- so first-one-wins is a coin toss between them even in the working case, and the wrong one produces the same silent failure with a plausible-looking address in the log. board_run::execute inherits the guess because it passes only --mac and --root
owner_path: Two changes, and the first is the load-bearing one. (1) tos64-netboot must REFUSE TO START rather than fall back to IPAddress.Any: a server that cannot name its own address cannot serve, and Any is not an address a client can TFTP from. Same shape as the LE-87 port guard -- refuse loudly rather than proceed half-configured. (2) When more than one link-local candidate exists, name them all and refuse rather than pick, per the same argument. (3) board_run::execute passes --server through, and board-run refuses without it. Note the ordering trap for whoever fixes this: the bench NIC has no link until the board is powered, so the address CANNOT be discovered at start time on the very run that needs it -- explicit is the only correct answer, not better guessing

summary: THE CANVAS WAS DARK ON A NETBOOTED RUN THAT WAS OTHERWISE COMPLETELY HEALTHY, AND NOTHING IN THE IMAGE CAN TELL. On 2026-08-06 the board fetched the right image (583 blocks, sha256 b6dbabae...), ran the fixture, reached the park loop and transmitted 89 spoor records with 0 lost and 0 refused plus a complete 14-metric envelope -- and the monitor showed nothing. Per hal-arm64::boot the park loop PAINTS AND TRANSMITS, and transmit is proven, so TinyOS was writing pixels the whole time and nothing was scanning them out. The cause is that SIMPLEFB_BASE = 0x3F800000 is HARDCODED from a Raspberry Pi OS capture (board.rs, STORY-P1-07-09, BND-03 -- there is still no device-tree parser) and NOTHING VERIFIES THE FIRMWARE ALLOCATED A FRAMEBUFFER THERE THIS BOOT. config.txt carries no hdmi_force_hotplug, so a monitor absent or asleep at power-on, or connected to HDMI1 rather than HDMI0, leaves the firmware with no display and TinyOS painting into RAM it does not own. THAT IS THE PART THAT IS NOT COSMETIC: this is a 4 MB write to a fixed physical address on a no-IOMMU machine, and safety precedes correctness in this project's ordering. It also contradicts nothing in STORY-P1-07-09, which records criterion 4 re-observed on 2026-08-05's NETBOOTED run (BOARD VERDICT 14) -- so the channel worked over netboot before and did not this time, and the difference has not been identified. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN: STORY-P1-09-16 criterion 4 reads the RX counters off the CANVAS and 04C deliberately kept them off the wire, so that criterion is blocked on the display rather than on the board
owner_path: DONE 2026-08-06 (09C), and it narrows the defect rather than closing it. The park loop now paints only when the firmware answered the native-size query: hdmi::show_splash returns a DisplayOutcome carrying BOTH answers instead of folding the size query into choose_mode and discarding it, hdmi::canvas_permitted is the one pure decision with its own tests, and canvas::SimplefbSurface has no public constructor -- canvas::Canvas::permitted_by is the only way to one, so a boot with no display cannot reach the write_volatile at all. The refusal is spoken (TOS64-CANVAS/1 painting=no reason=firmware-reported-no-display) because a surface that refuses silently is LE-87s shape. NOT gated on the framebuffer GRANT deliberately: this firmware refuses that (fb=refused, BOARD VERDICT 4), so gating on it would delete the only display path the project owns -- there is a test asserting exactly that, because it is the mistake the obvious fix makes. WHAT REMAINS, and it is why this row stays open. (1) The ADDRESS is still SIMPLEFB_BASE from a Raspberry Pi OS capture with no device-tree parser behind it (BND-03): a display existing is not a framebuffer existing AT THAT ADDRESS this boot, so the unjustified write is narrowed from every boot to boots where a panel is reported, not eliminated. A device-tree parse is the fix that ends the argument. (2) The FAULT path still paints without evidence, deliberately and named at canvas::Canvas::last_resort_for_fault_report: it can run before the splash has asked, and serial has never produced a byte on this bench (LE-47), so a fault that paints nothing is a board that hangs with no symptom. That is a trade of one hazard against a worse one, not a justification. (3) Unverified on hardware -- no board run has happened since; hdmi_force_hotplug=1 and HDMI0 still want one power cycle. (4) STORY-P1-09-16 criterion 4 reads RX counters off the canvas and stays blocked until (3)

summary: THE SHIPPING DISPATCH ROUND IS OVER PERF-D05-G23'\''S PER-ROUND STAMP BUDGET BY 3.3x, AND THE ONLY THING MAKING THAT HARMLESS IS THE 1 Hz PARK BEAT. Measured 2026-08-06 on silicon and filed as PERF-D05-G23: one spoor stamp costs 110 cycles at p99 on a 1650-cycle cooperative dispatch round, so G23'\''s 2 percent allowance admits one stamp per ~3.3 rounds and kernel::board_dispatch::tinyos_dispatch_round stamps ONCE PER ROUND on every exit. This is NOT a fixture artefact -- the fixture arm and the shipping site are the same construction (Scheduler capacity 4, one task at priority 11, WcetBudgetTicks(1000), yield-forever, dispatch::run_once, one stamp inside), which is why PERF-D07-G23'\''s no-denominator-in-shipping-code escape does not transfer to D05. It is harmless TODAY only because hal_arm64::ethernet'\''s park loop waits 100 ms per tick and runs its stamping body on every tenth tick, so exactly one round executes per second: 110 cycles per second on a 2.4 GHz core, about one part in 22 million, and the gate'\''s CPU-cycles clause passes by seven orders of magnitude while its p99 clause fails by 3.3x. THE DEBT IS THAT NOTHING GUARDS THE ASSUMPTION. No test, no gate and no comment ties the park beat to this budget, so raising the beat, adding a second stamped call site inside the round, or landing the preemptive scheduler D05 readiness already anticipates would breach the ratio silently and with no symptom on the wire
owner_path: CLOSED 2026-08-06 (09C) by three host tests, each falsified by mutation rather than assumed. hal_arm64::ethernet: PARK_TICK_MS/PARK_BEAT_TICKS/PARK_BEAT_MS are named constants the loop actually uses, a test asserts the beat is 1 Hz with a message naming PERF-D05-G23, a source-level test asserts the loop paces itself from the constants rather than literals beside them, and a third counts exactly one dispatch round in the beat body. kernel::board_dispatch: STAMPS_PER_DISPATCH_ROUND plus a source-level test asserting stamps = exits = three, one stamp per round on every path -- source-level because tinyos_dispatch_round drives a real context switch through statics and no host can call it and count. Neither guard encodes a measured figure; the cycle costs belong to a boot, not to a design constant. WHAT THE GUARD CANNOT SEE, stated because a closed row that reads as fully guarded is worse than an open one. (1) The transitive check is one module deep: it asserts dispatch.rs contains no stamp in shipped code, which covers run_once because that is the only thing the round enters that could reach the journal -- a stamp added two modules down, or reached through a trait object or function pointer, is invisible to a text scan and always will be. (2) Both scans are TEXT. A stamp emitted by a macro, or by generated code, counts zero. (3) The needle is the bare identifier so an unqualified call after a use is caught, but a renaming re-export would not be. (4) The exits count is whitespace-pinned and a reindent reddens the test -- that fails LOUD and is the acceptable direction. Reviewed 2026-08-06 after two rounds of review found the callee and unqualified-call holes, both now closed and both mutation-tested; the residue above is what remains and it is a text scan is not a call graph. The over-budget ratio itself is not a loose end -- it is PERF-D05-G23 row, where it belongs

summary: CI RUNS NO TESTS AT ALL, so every host unit test in this repository gates a developer's own machine and the pre-commit hook and NOTHING on the runner. .github/workflows/ci.yml has four jobs; the governance one runs fmt, clippy --all-targets, three xtask checks and cargo doc, and the other three boot QEMU fixtures. There is no cargo test step anywhere in the file. clippy --all-targets COMPILES the test harnesses, which is why this looks covered at a glance and is the reason it has survived: a broken test fails the build, a FAILING test does not. Roughly 1210 host tests were passing locally when this was found, including every source-level guard filed as the closure of a loose end -- LE-99's stamp density, LE-97's cadence, the G23 pair equivalence, check-citations' the_committed_tree_has_no_unresolved_citation. Each of those was written as the mechanism that stops a defect recurring and each is invisible to the runner. GENERAL SHAPE: a gate is only as strong as the weakest place it is actually executed, and this project has repeatedly filed a #[test] as a closure without checking that CI runs it (LE-72 and LE-92 are the same discovery for two compile targets; this is the same discovery for the test runner)

owner_path: Add a host test job to ci.yml. NOT a one-line addition to the governance job: the suite needs the same pinned toolchain and takes long enough that it belongs beside the QEMU jobs rather than in front of the fast deterministic gates that exist to fail in seconds. Decide deliberately whether a failure is blocking on day one -- it should be, but the first run may surface tests that pass on Windows and fail on Linux, which is LE-64's family and must not be discovered as a surprise mid-merge. Until it lands, treat every #[test]-only closure in loose-ends.tsv as locally enforced only, and prefer an xtask subcommand wired into ci.yml for anything filed as a mechanism -- which is what check-metric-labels does for LE-91. CLOSED 2026-08-06 (14D) by a host-tests job in ci.yml running cargo test --workspace -- its own job beside the QEMU ones, blocking from day one, so the 1228 host tests that gated nothing on the runner now fail the build. The MECHANISM half is xtask check-ci-gates, wired into the governance job AND the pre-commit hook, because the obvious guard is circular and therefore worthless: a #[test] asserting CI runs the host tests is executed by the very job it asserts the existence of and dies with it. It refuses four things -- no suite at all, a suite inside governance-gates where the seconds-fast gates would queue behind it, a non-blocking or exit-code-swallowing suite, and any check named in ci_gates::CI_ENFORCED missing from the workflow, itself included. VERIFIED BY MUTATING THE COMMITTED WORKFLOW RATHER THAN A FIXTURE, which is the only reason the broken first version was caught: narrowing run: cargo test --workspace to cargo test -p kernel while the step's own - name: still quoted the full command left this gate GREEN, because the scan matched a display name. That is 12D's lesson landing on its own author -- the mutation that mattered was the one that made the gate stay SILENT, run against the exact case it was written for. The parser now treats only run: values and block-scalar bodies as executable; five real-file mutations each fail with the ERROR read rather than the exit code, and the name-only case is pinned by a fixture test. RESIDUAL, STATED: this gate proves the workflow ASKS for the suite, never that a runner passed it, and the first Linux runs may still surface tests that pass on this Windows bench -- LE-64's family, and the reason this landed alone rather than inside a merge

(2) THE ACCOUNT-LEVEL CANDIDATE IS RULED OUT ON STRUCTURE RATHER THAN ON A PROBE. 01A pointed at an Actions spending limit or billing state and recorded it unresolved because the session token lacked the scope. That scope is moot twice over: users/revred/settings/billing/actions now returns HTTP 410 with endpoint has been moved, and more decisively revred/TinyOS is PUBLIC (private:false) with every job on ubuntu-latest, a standard runner -- standard runners on public repositories are unmetered, so no spending limit can suppress them. Confirmed live alongside it: actions/permissions enabled:true allowed_actions:all, both workflows state:active. One correction to 10C ruled-out list, which changes no conclusion but should not be inherited: .github/ was NOT untouched -- e273931 and dff7b1d both edit ci.yml. It changes nothing because the EARLIEST silent push, b4a7010, touched no workflow file at all. fork-advisories silence over the same window is explained by its paths filter (.gitmodules and its own file) and is not evidence either way. (3) THE INSTRUMENT, AND THIS IS THE PART TO KEEP. 01A reported that actions/runs?head_sha= returns 0 regardless and therefore ruled nothing out. That is half right and the correction is sharper than the claim: the probe works, but ONLY when fed a full 40-character SHA. head_sha=420e875 returns total_count 0; head_sha=420e8758c94c1296e5e088c1d6a84db87f0b1115 returns 1, for the same run. 10C abbreviated the SHA, so its probe was not answering a question about the run at all -- it was answering, correctly, about a commit identifier the API accepts and never matches. LE-80 family for the fourth time in four sessions, and it extends 01A own rule: checking that an instrument CAN return both answers is not enough if it can be handed an argument it accepts and silently cannot match.
